text: Hlengiwe Buhle Mkhize (6 September 1952 – 16 September 2021) was a South African politician who served as Minister of Higher Education and Training and Minister of Home Affairs under President Jacob Zuma. A member of the National Assembly and national executive since May 2009, she was Deputy Minister in the Presidency for Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities when she died in September 2021. Born on 6 September 1952, she completed a Bachelor of Arts in psychology, social work, and sociology at the University of Zululand in 1976, where she was involved in student activism. She earned an Honours in psychology in 1978 and a Master's in clinical psychology in 1981, both from the University of Natal. Mkhize spent over a decade in academia as a senior lecturer at the University of Zululand from 1984 to 1990 and at the University of the Witwatersrand from 1990 to 1995, and also served as a visiting professor at the University of Illinois and University of Mississippi. In 1995, she was appointed to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, where she chaired the Reparations and Rehabilitation Committee, and held various civil society roles, including establishing the National Children and Violence Trust, serving as a reparations officer in the President's Fund, chairing the South African branch of Transparency International, and leading the University of Zululand’s council. She also had business interests, being a director in 15 private companies, including Aerosud, by the time she joined government in 2009. A long-serving member of the African National Congress (ANC), she served in her local branch executive from 1991 to 2004 and was national treasurer of the ANC Women's League from July 2008 to August 2015, during which she raised over R40-million in funds. She was elected to the National Assembly in the April 2009 general election, representing the ANC, and was re-elected in 2014 and 2019, serving until her death in 2021. In 2005, President Thabo Mbeki appointed her as South African Ambassador to the Netherlands, a post she held until 2008, during which she chaired the executive council of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons and was vice-president of the International Criminal Court from 2006 to 2008. Between 2009 and 2017, she served as deputy minister in four portfolios: Deputy Minister of Correctional Services (2009–2010), Deputy Minister of Higher Education and Training (2010–2012), Deputy Minister of Economic Development (2012–2014), and Deputy Minister of Telecommunications and Postal Services (2014–2017). In February 2018, she was sacked by President Cyril Ramaphosa, who succeeded Jacob Zuma, and retreated to the Portfolio Committee on Communications, where she was elected chair in November 2018 and served until after the May 2019 general election. After the 2019 election, she was appointed Deputy Minister in the Presidency for Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities, deputising Minister Maite Nkoana-Mashabane, and served until her death. She was first elected to the National Executive Committee of the ANC in 2017, ranking 73rd out of 80 ordinary members. Mkhize was diagnosed with lung cancer in March 2017 and was hospitalised on 31 August 2021. She died in hospital in Johannesburg on 16 December 2021, aged 69. President Ramaphosa granted her an official funeral. She was married to Pat Mkhize and had four children – three daughters and a son – and a grandson. She was also chairperson of the June and Andrew Mlangeni Foundation.
